description: The size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for.

a.request: Using spatial records (`scanspatial`) matched to a project (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), for each funding source (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) compute the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and the number of distinct projects. Keep the funding sources whose number of distinct projects is above the average of that number across all funding sources. Return one row with: the average of the kept sources' ratios; the total of their distinct project counts; and the average amount by which their counts exceed the cross-source average. No rounding.
a.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS fundflux, AVG(s.boxy / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS n_proj FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), a AS (SELECT AVG(n_proj * 1.0) AS avg_n FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio_of_kept, SUM(g.n_proj) AS total_distinct_projects, AVG(g.n_proj - a.avg_n) AS avg_excess FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.n_proj > a.avg_n

c.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and how big it is. For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding. The size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for.
c.sql: WITH src AS (SELECT p.fundflux, AVG(s.boxy * 1.0 / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS sz FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), av AS (SELECT AVG(sz * 1.0) AS a FROM src) SELECT AVG(src.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_ratios, SUM(src.sz) AS combined_size, AVG(src.sz - av.a) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM src CROSS JOIN av WHERE src.sz > av.a

b.request: Group the spatial scan records by project funding source (a missing source counts as its own group), and size each source by the number of distinct projects with spatial data. Then, among the sources whose size is above the average size across all sources, return one row with the average of their per-source mean `boxy`/`boxz` ratios (missing values ignored), their combined size, and the average amount by which their sizes exceed the average size, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.fundflux, COUNT(DISTINCT s.arcref) AS sz, AVG(s.boxy * 1.0 / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS r FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), a AS (SELECT AVG(sz * 1.0) AS av FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.r) AS avg_mean_ratio, SUM(g.sz) AS combined_size, AVG(g.sz - a.av) AS avg_excess FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.sz > a.av

d.request: Looking at spatial scan data (`scanspatial`) linked to projects (`projects.arcregistry` = `scanspatial.arcref`), which funding sources (`projects.fundflux`, treating a missing source as its own group) are bigger than average, where the size of each funding source is measured by how many distinct projects it has spatial data for? For each funding source, work out the average ratio of bounding box Y (`boxy`) to bounding box Z (`boxz`), ignoring missing values, and its size (the number of distinct projects with spatial data). For the sources above the average size across funding sources, give one row with the average of their ratios, their combined size, and how far on average they exceed the average size. No rounding.
d.sql: WITH src AS (SELECT p.fundflux AS fundflux, AVG(s.boxy * 1.0 / NULLIF(s.boxz, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) AS size FROM scanspatial s JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref GROUP BY p.fundflux), avgsize AS (SELECT AVG(size * 1.0) AS a FROM src) SELECT AVG(src.avg_ratio) AS average_ratio, SUM(src.size) AS combined_size, AVG(src.size - avgsize.a) AS average_excess FROM src CROSS JOIN avgsize WHERE src.size > avgsize.a
